findings: brand: 4 of 4 frames correct against ground truth (Kirkland Signature), including the two frames where the model gave name:null -- brand was legible on the label in every frame, name text was not.

name: 2 of 4 frames correct (Natural Spring Water, matching ground truth's 'Natural spring water' up to case), 2 of 4 frames returned null rather than guessing -- in both null cases, the actual product-name text was outside the photographed crop (barcode/recycling-text close-ups). This is the null-for-unreadable instruction working as asked, not a disagreement to average away.

sizeValue/sizeUnit/netQuantityText: null in all 4 of 4 frames, despite the real product having a printed '500 mL' on its label. None of the four real shutter frames used here happened to have that text inside the photographed crop. This means a photo-only extract pass, at least from this app's real capture angles, frequently cannot recover size on its own -- consistent with why the app also matches by barcode against the catalogue rather than relying on the photo alone for size.
no search chip or grounded citation appeared on any of the four frames, confirming the ungrounded-prompt request stayed ungrounded on the website UI for this prompt style.
